label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (OpenCode)
explanation: Gated rank-1 residual steering toward a Python-code answer mode. Diagnosis: on the unedited model, held-out-style coding prompts failed mostly through (a) drifting to non-Python code (wrote C/Java) and (b) noisy prose/multiple-alternative code blocks; the underlying Python ability is present (forcing a Python fence prefix yields correct code). Internals: teacher-forced/lens analysis showed the fence-language decision is encoded as a residual-stream direction at late layers; activation patching a Python-framed fence context into a C-framed one at resid.20/22/23 flips the next token from c to python (KL~12), while resid.15 does not. Construction (no gradients): per module A = g^T is the coding-request gate direction (mean coding-prompt input minus mean general-prompt input at the assistant-start), B = s*u where u is the unit Python-minus-(C,Java) residual direction at resid.21/resid.23 obtained by differencing forced-framing traces. Applied to model.layers.20/22 linear_attn.out_proj and mlp.down_proj (4 rank-1 modules; ||dW||/||W|| between 0.5% and 1.3%). Selectivity comes from the gate: at a coding assistant-start the added residual norm is ~4.0 of the ~9 resid norm, while for general/chat prompts it is only ~0.6 with mixed sign, so non-coding abilities are barely perturbed.
